subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application Which statement correctly describes the direction of RNA synthesis during transcription?

options.text: RNA polymerase adds ribonucleotides to the 5' end of the growing RNA, so RNA is made 3' to 5'.
RNA polymerase adds each ribonucleotide to the 3' end of the growing chain, so RNA is made 5' to 3'.
The RNA transcript has the same sequence as the template strand it was copied from.
RNA polymerase requires a short primer before it can begin RNA synthesis.

explanation: RNA polymerase adds each new ribonucleotide to the 3' hydroxyl of the growing chain, so the RNA is synthesized 5' to 3', antiparallel to the template strand. A states the reverse direction, a classic orientation error. C is wrong because the template strand is complementary to the RNA, while the coding strand matches it. D is wrong because transcription, unlike DNA replication, does not need a primer.
